context: The result in Corollary 1.6 has applications to Connected Obstacle Removal, in particular, to the interesting case when the obstacles are convex polygons, each intersecting a constant number of other polygons. The question about the complexity of this problem was posed in [9, 11], and remains open. The result in Corollary 1.6 implies that this problem is FPT. We finally mention that it remains open whether Colored Path-Con and Connected Obstacle Removal are FPT parameterized by k only. 2 Preliminaries We assume familiarity with graph theory and parameterized complexity. We refer the reader to the standard books [5, 6]. For a set S, we denote by 2S the power set of S. Let G = (V, E) be a graph, let C ⊂ N be a finite set of colors, and let χ : V −→ 2C . A vertex v in V is empty if χ(v) = ∅. A color S c appears on, or is contained in, a subset S of vertices if c ∈ v∈S χ(v). For two vertices Sr u, v ∈ V (G), ` ∈ N, a u-v path P = (u = v0 , . . . , vr = v) in G is `-valid if | i=0 χ(vi )| ≤ `; that is, if the total number of colors appearing on the vertices of P is at most `. A color S c ∈ C is connected in G, or simply connected, if c∈χ(v) {v} induces a connected subgraph of G. The graph G is color-connected, if for every c ∈ C, c is connected in G.
